_about: Candidate response actions for brick/block masonry delay risks, transcribed from Research_Notes/D_mitigation.md section 6 (mitigation measure -> quantified evidence -> what still requires expert/user input); C-TRANSFER comes from the response-taxonomy row of that table (avoid, reduce, transfer, absorb). It lists WHAT could be done and WHAT MUST BE ELICITED. It contains no effect sizes and no costs: D_mitigation.md section 7 found that no paper supplies a transferable risk-reduction factor for a masonry-specific mitigation, so every p_after, delay_after and cost must come from the user or an expert, with a Source. 'evidence_ids' point to records in the evidence store (D## notes) and give plausibility context only. 'applies_to' is the project team's mapping of the measure to library risk ids (data/risk_library_masonry.json), not a claim made by the papers.

entries.mechanism: Holds enough bricks, blocks and mortar materials on site (or schedules delivery just in time) so a late delivery does not stop the gang.
entries.evidence_summary: Only inside a bundle (D03: task duration reduced about 30%, PPC about 55% to 80%). D11 shows an optimum buffer size with no numbers; D34 and D18 are models. No stand-alone masonry effect located.
inputs_required: probability of the material-shortage event after the action
carrying cost of the extra stock
secondary risk: storage or weather damage
secondary_risks_to_consider: Damage, theft or weather loss of stored material
entries.note: Benefit is non-monotonic: a very large buffer adds storage and damage risk (D11). Model it as such.

entries.mechanism: A second approved supplier reduces dependence on one source for bricks, blocks or mortar.
entries.evidence_summary: Not located. D35 gives direction only for material availability and selection time.
inputs_required: probability and delay after the action (expert-elicited)
secondary risk: quality variation between suppliers

entries.mechanism: Orders and takes delivery of masonry materials ahead of need, removing exposure to lead-time and price changes.
entries.evidence_summary: No delay-effect number located (D35 direction only; D17 cost-saving figures come from an optimisation model for advance payment). D01 reports material unavailability as the top cause of failed assignments in an Indian case.
inputs_required: probability and delay after the action
capital or financing cost of early purchase
secondary risk: storage damage or theft

entries.mechanism: Adds masons and helpers so the activity recovers days lost to shortage or low output.
entries.evidence_summary: Only the congestion side effect is quantified in simulation (D12). D10, D25 and D18 are context.
secondary_risks_to_consider: Work-front congestion and lower productivity per worker

entries.mechanism: Extends working hours or adds a shift to recover lost time.
entries.evidence_summary: D09 reports a productivity loss range for shift work with an ambiguous sign convention in the abstract; D07 found moderate occasional overtime not significant; D08 direction only.
inputs_required: secondary risks: fatigue, rework and safety
entries.note: D10 and D37 link overtime to rework and fatigue, so a secondary risk should normally be added.

entries.mechanism: Replaces part of the hand bricklaying with larger blocks, interlocking units or prefabricated panels.
entries.evidence_summary: D04 (laboratory, interlocking masonry), D05 (survey, IBS) and D06 (prefabrication, New Zealand) report productivity or time gains in other contexts. AAC versus clay-brick productivity in local conditions: not located.
inputs_required: cracking or rework risk from the change
secondary_risks_to_consider: Cracking or rework from mortar or block change
entries.note: Evidence is context only; none of it is a masonry-in-India effect size.

entries.mechanism: Improves workmanship and speed of the existing gang through instruction and supervision.
inputs_required: effect on productivity and rework probability

entries.mechanism: Ties part of pay to output so the gang works steadily and attendance improves.
entries.evidence_summary: D27: incentives accounted for 6% to 26% of the variation in output (variance explained, not a productivity gain). D01: single case where PPC peaked after a bonus was introduced.
inputs_required: incentive cost per unit of work
entries.note: Do not read D27's percentage as a productivity gain.

entries.mechanism: Re-plans brick and mortar staging, hoist position and work zones to cut handling and waiting.
entries.evidence_summary: D03 (bundle including layout) and D12 (work zones reduced simulated spatial conflicts). Masonry-only effect: not located.
inputs_required: local productivity or delay change for masonry

entries.mechanism: Covers fresh work, plans indoor or sheltered work during heavy rain, or re-sequences the activity around the monsoon.
entries.evidence_summary: No mitigation effect size located. D20 gives hazard size only (one Kolkata housing project); D26 gives heat effects in Oman; D14 lists seasonal scheduling as a response without a separable effect.
inputs_required: residual delay after covering or rescheduling
secondary risk: schedule compression after the monsoon
secondary_risks_to_consider: Schedule compression after the rainy period

entries.mechanism: Adds inspection hold points and checklists before the next course so defects are caught early.
entries.evidence_summary: Not located for masonry. D03 reports rework incidents 15 to 12 inside a lean bundle only.
inputs_required: rework probability and rework days per defect type

entries.mechanism: Weekly planning with look-ahead and constraint removal so work packages are ready before the gang arrives.
entries.evidence_summary: PPC improvements reported in India (D01, D02, D30) and Canada (D03). PPC is a reliability measure, not delay: no paper except D02's weak '12-20%' converts it into delay days or probability.
inputs_required: conversion of the PPC change into probability and delay after the action (expert judgement)
entries.note: Do not treat a PPC gain as a delay reduction.

entries.measure: Transfer to a subcontractor or supplier (contractual)
entries.mechanism: Moves delivery or workmanship responsibility to a party with a contractual penalty for late performance.
entries.evidence_summary: Response taxonomy only (avoid, reduce, transfer, absorb: D14, D16). No masonry effect size located.
entries.note: Cost of the premium and the enforceability of the penalty are contract-specific.
